Lattice Multiplication

ArithmeticAlgorithmsCounting
Game: Multiply two numbers by filling a lattice and adding along its diagonals.
How to play: Change either factor. Each cell shows part of a product, and the band sums give the answer.

Look for the math

Before calculators, a grid of small products could turn a big multiplication into simple addition.

Filling the lattice

Write one factor over the columns and the other beside the rows. Each cell holds the product of its two digits, with the tens above the diagonal and the units below. For 712 × 23 the cells are 14, 21, 02, 03, 04 and 06.

Bands and carries

Add the digits along each diagonal band, from the bottom-right upwards. The page's 1, 6, 3, 7, 6 gives 16376 directly. When a band reaches two digits, carry its tens to the band on the left: 124576 × 3857 has a band sum of 10, which becomes 480489632 after carrying. The logic test checks 1,000 random pairs against ordinary multiplication.

Find two factors whose band sums are all under ten, so no carrying is needed.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
